subject: Spanska
title: Grammar: present tense of regular verbs
sourceSummary: Present tense conjugation of -ar, -er, and -ir verbs, plus the irregular verbs ser and estar.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Yo ___ español." (hablar = to speak)
questions.opener: -ar verbs in the present tense end in -o for "yo".
questions.explanation: "Hablar" is an -ar verb: yo hablo, tú hablas, él/ella habla, ellos hablan. "Yo" gives the ending -o: "hablo".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Ella ___ en Madrid." (vivir = to live)
questions.opener: -ir verbs in the present tense end in -e for "él/ella".
questions.explanation: "Vivir" is an -ir verb: yo vivo, tú vives, él/ella vive, ellos viven. "Ella" gives the ending -e: "vive".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Nosotros ___ mucho en clase." (aprender = to learn)
questions.opener: -er verbs in the present tense end in -emos for "nosotros".
questions.explanation: "Aprender" is an -er verb: nosotros aprendemos. The ending -emos is used for "we".

questions.prompt: Choose the right verb: "Mi hermana ___ alta." (My sister is tall.)
questions.opener: Ser is used for traits that don't change, like height.
questions.explanation: "Ser" is used for permanent traits (appearance, personality, profession): "es alta" = "is tall". "Estar" is instead used for temporary states or location, e.g. "está cansada" (is tired right now).

questions.prompt: Choose the right verb: "¿Dónde ___ el baño?" (Where is the bathroom?)
questions.opener: Estar is used to say where something is located.
questions.explanation: "Estar" is used for location: "¿Dónde está...?" = "Where is...?". "Ser" would instead be used for e.g. time or identity, not location.

questions.prompt: Write the Spanish word for "you all" (several people you're speaking to).
questions.opener: The equivalent of the English "you (plural)" in the informal form.

questions.prompt: Correct the two errors: "Yo vive en Suecia y tú hablo inglés muy bien."
questions.opener: Check which person each verb actually belongs to.
questions.answer: Yo vivo en Suecia y tú hablas inglés muy bien.
steps: "Yo vive" → "Yo vivo". The verb vivir conjugates for "I" (yo) as "vivo", not "vive" (which is for he/she).
"Tú hablo" → "Tú hablas". The verb hablar conjugates for "you" (tú) as "hablas", not "hablo" (which is for I).
Read the sentence again: "Yo vivo en Suecia y tú hablas inglés muy bien" means "I live in Sweden and you speak English very well."

questions.prompt: How are -ar, -er, and -ir verbs conjugated in the present tense, and when do you use ser versus estar?
questions.opener: The three verb groups follow different but regular patterns.
questions.answer: -ar (hablar): hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan. -er (aprender): aprendo, aprendes, aprende, aprendemos, aprendéis, aprenden. -ir (vivir): vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven. Ser is used for permanent things: yo soy, tú eres, él/ella es, nosotros somos, ellos son — e.g. appearance, profession, nationality. Estar is used for location and temporary states: yo estoy, tú estás, él/ella está, nosotros estamos, ellos están — e.g. where something is, or how someone feels right now.
